name: Nimzo-Indian Defense
description: Pin the c3 knight with …Bb4 and fight for e4: flexible and very sound.

lines.name: 4.Qc2 (Classical)

notes.3: …e6 frees the f8 bishop and prepares …Bb4 or …d5.
notes.5: …Bb4 pins the c3 knight, so White can't easily play e4.
notes.6: Qc2 avoids doubled pawns after …Bxc3, taking back with the queen.
notes.11: …b6 prepares …Bb7 to control e4 and the long diagonal.

lines.summary: Against Qc2, castle; after a3 give the bishop on c3 and fight for e4 with …b6 and …Bb7.

lines.name: 4.Qc2 O-O 5.e4

notes.3: …e6 frees the f8 bishop and prepares …Bb4 or …d5.
notes.5: …Bb4 pins the c3 knight, so White can't easily play e4.
notes.6: Qc2 avoids doubled pawns after …Bxc3, taking back with the queen.
notes.9: …d5 hits e4 at once, before White's centre gets going.

9.Bxc3+: bxc3 gives White a big centre; hit e4 with …d5 first.

lines.summary: If White grabs the centre with e4, strike back at once with …d5.

notes.3: …e6 frees the f8 bishop and prepares …Bb4 or …d5.
notes.5: …Bb4 pins the c3 knight, so White can't easily play e4.
notes.6: Qc2 avoids doubled pawns after …Bxc3, taking back with the queen.

lines.name: 4.Nf3

notes.3: …e6 frees the f8 bishop and prepares …Bb4 or …d5.
notes.5: …Bb4 pins the c3 knight, so White can't easily play e4.
notes.7: …O-O: castle first and keep all options: …d5, …c5 or …b6.

lines.summary: Against the quiet 4.Nf3, castle first and decide later between …d5, …c5 and …b6.

lines.name: 4.Bg5 (Leningrad)

notes.3: …e6 frees the f8 bishop and prepares …Bb4 or …d5.
notes.5: …Bb4 pins the c3 knight, so White can't easily play e4.
notes.9: …c5 hits d4; the pin on c3 makes it hard for White to keep the centre.

lines.summary: Against 4.Bg5, kick the bishop with …h6 and hit d4 with …c5.

lines.name: 4.e3 (Rubinstein)

notes.3: …e6 frees the f8 bishop and prepares …Bb4 or …d5.
notes.5: …Bb4 pins the c3 knight, so White can't easily play e4.
notes.9: …d5 claims the centre; …c5 and …Nc6 come next.

lines.summary: Against 4.e3, castle and take the centre with …d5, then …c5 and …Nc6.

lines.name: 4.e3 O-O 5.Bd3 d5 6.Nf3

notes.3: …e6 frees the f8 bishop and prepares …Bb4 or …d5.
notes.5: …Bb4 pins the c3 knight, so White can't easily play e4.
notes.9: …d5 claims the centre; …c5 and …Nc6 come next.
notes.11: …c5 adds pressure on d4; the pin on c3 is still annoying for White.

lines.summary: The Rubinstein main line: …d5, …c5 and …Nc6, with pressure on d4 and c4.

lines.name: 4.Bd2

notes.3: …e6 frees the f8 bishop and prepares …Bb4 or …d5.
notes.5: …Bb4 pins the c3 knight, so White can't easily play e4.
notes.7: …O-O: the bishop on d2 is passive, so Black simply castles.

lines.summary: Against the modest 4.Bd2, castle and play …d5 or …c5.

lines.name: 4.a3 (Samisch)

notes.3: …e6 frees the f8 bishop and prepares …Bb4 or …d5.
notes.5: …Bb4 pins the c3 knight, so White can't easily play e4.
notes.7: …Bxc3+ doubles White's c-pawns; that's the point of the pin.
notes.9: …c5 fixes the doubled pawns and pressures d4.

lines.summary: When a3 asks the bishop, take on c3 and aim at the doubled c-pawns with …c5.

lines.name: 3.Nf3 Bb4+

notes.3: …e6 frees the f8 bishop and prepares …Bb4 or …d5.
notes.5: …Bb4+: the same bishop check idea, even without a knight on c3.
notes.7: …Bxd2+ trades the bishop for White's good bishop and simplifies.

lines.summary: When White avoids Nc3, give the check anyway and trade bishops on d2.
